content.title: About
content.content: The chicken, rice & cheese burrito is a Mexican‑style dish consisting of a large soft wheat tortilla filled with seasoned grilled chicken, steamed rice, shredded cheese and often topped with salsa or sour cream. This combination provides a balanced mix of protein, carbohydrates and fats.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Burritos originated in northern Mexico where wheat flour tortillas were more common than corn.
Chicken is usually marinated in chili, cumin and lime for a distinctive flavor.
Mexican‑style rice is often cooked with tomato sauce and a hint of spices, giving it a richer taste.
Cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese melts smoothly, creating a creamy texture inside the burrito.
Because it is handheld, the burrito became a staple of fast‑food chains worldwide.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Sustained energy
items.content: Rice supplies complex carbohydrates that release energy slowly, helping you stay full longer.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Cheese adds calcium and phosphorus, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both chicken and rice contain B6 and B12 vitamins, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Adding vegetables such as lettuce or tomatoes boosts fiber content, beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Large burritos can be high in calories due to the tortilla, cheese and sauces, which should be considered in weight management.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cheese and ready‑made sauces often contain salt; choose low‑sodium options if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or dairy protein allergy.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: Chicken must be cooked to an internal temperature of 75 °C (165 °F) to prevent salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The burrito is designed to be handheld; warm it in the microwave or on a skillet until the cheese melts. Serve with salsa, guacamole or sour cream to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared burrito in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For freezing, wrap tightly in plastic film and keep for up to 2 months; reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.
